Child Helpline (CHL) is a 24-hour

emergency toll free number (1098) providing

rehabilitation services. It is a response

e. Child Protection Committees

Child Protection Committees (CPCs) have

been established as a grassroots mechanism for

identification of vulnerable children, prevention of

child rights violations and timely referral for care

and protection. At present, 12,938 committees

have been constituted across Tamil Nadu at

various levels. Apart from District level CPCs, in

urban areas, Child Protection Committees are

constituted at the corporation zonal, corporation

ward, municipality, municipality ward, town

panchayat, and town panchayat ward levels. In

rural areas, CPCs are constituted at the block and

village levels. The Committees address issues

including child marriage, child labour, trafficking,

illegal adoption, sexual offences against children,

female infanticide and other violations of child

rights. Quarterly meetings are conducted where

the children related issues are discussed and

appropriate actions are initiated.

94

f. Tamil Nadu Commission for Protection of Child rights

The Tamil Nadu Commission for Protection

of Child Rights (TNCPCR) is a statutory body

established to safeguard and promote the rights,

safety, and welfare of children in the State. The

Commission consists of one chairperson and six

members, who are appointed by the Government.

It plays an important role in ensuring that

children receive proper care, protection, and

access to their rights.

The Commission monitors the

implementation of child-related laws, including

the JJ Act, POCSO Act and Right to Education Act.

Finance Department - Revenue Augmentation Committee - To suggest measures for sustainable augmentation of State's Tax and Non-Tax revenues — Constituted - Orders - Issued.

FINANCE (FDAU) DEPARTMENT

G.O.(Ms.) No.148 Dated:24.07.2026 LITTLICU, SL19-8, FHoauctEHpeuy 2,60o1G)- 2057

ORDER:

The White Paper on fiscal management of Tamil Nadu that was published in June 2026 sets the roadmap for better revenue mobilisation and administrative reforms, and has inter alia observed that the decline across major taxes like GST, VAT, and excise including revenues from mines and minerals has been mainly driven by administrative choices, leakages and corruption in the past rather than an underlying economic slowdown. It has also indicated that resolving this shortfall requires long-term, multi-year reforms focused on curbing corruption, enforcing compliance, and mobilizing resources efficiently. Some of the key factors highlighted in the White Paper are outlined below:

e Own-tax effort at a historic low — the SOTR-to-GSDP ratio fell to 5.45% in 2025-26, the lowest in two decades showing the sharpest decline among peer States in recent years.

e Large revenue foregone — decline in SOTR amounts to about Rs.1.23 lakh crore of annual revenue foregone, roughly 90% of the fiscal deficit in 2025-26.

e Unique to Tamil Nadu — Peer States like Maharashtra, and Karnataka have held on or have shown growth in SoTR-GSDP ratio, while Tamil Nadu alone has registered a steady decline.

e Broad-based weakness — the fall is reflected in all major taxes: GST, VAT on petroleum, State Excise, Stamp Duty and Motor Vehicle Tax.

e Cause is administrative, not structural — attributed to leakages, systemic corruption and administrative choices, primarily in commercial taxes, registration, excise and mining.

The White Paper on fiscal management of Tamil Nadu that was published in June 2026 sets the roadmap for better revenue mobilisation and administrative reforms, and has inter alia observed that the decline across major taxes like GST, VAT, and excise including revenues from mines and minerals has been mainly driven by administrative choices, leakages and corruption in the past rather than an underlying economic slowdown. It has also indicated that resolving this shortfall requires long-term, multi-year reforms focused on curbing corruption, enforcing compliance, and mobilizing resources efficiently. Some of the key factors highlighted in the White Paper are outlined below:

e Own-tax effort at a historic low — the SOTR-to-GSDP ratio fell to 5.45% in 2025-26, the lowest in two decades showing the sharpest decline among peer States in recent years.

e Large revenue foregone — decline in SOTR amounts to about Rs.1.23 lakh crore of annual revenue foregone, roughly 90% of the fiscal deficit in 2025-26.

e Unique to Tamil Nadu — Peer States like Maharashtra, and Karnataka have held on or have shown growth in SoTR-GSDP ratio, while Tamil Nadu alone has registered a steady decline.

e Broad-based weakness — the fall is reflected in all major taxes: GST, VAT on petroleum, State Excise, Stamp Duty and Motor Vehicle Tax.

e Cause is administrative, not structural — attributed to leakages, systemic corruption and administrative choices, primarily in commercial taxes, registration, excise and mining.
